# Lectures on Comparative Anatomy, delivered at the Royal College of Surgeons in 1843

The scan’s opening title names lectures delivered by Richard Owen, notes taken by William White Cooper and revision by Owen; Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, London, 1843. The E5 programme names the invertebrate-animal lectures. The selected witness is this 394-page scan, whose glossary supplies the consumed definitions. The opening title and embedded text at printed pp.374 and 379 were checked; no full-volume reading or image-level quotation transcription is claimed.

[Acquired witness](https://darwin-online.org.uk/converted/pdf/1843_Owen_Lectures_A5436.pdf). Retrieved and selected text checked on 8 September 2026. Local SHA-256: `335ae0d425f2ba241794052b7f66228ceb77fe59dee07ccf35d8ea1c2aa5025b`.

The witness **sources** [the historical branch](../../../../etymologies/homology-and-analogy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md) and **qualifies** the historical comparison in its [whole-field](../../../../etymologies/homology-and-analogy/WHOLE-FIELD.md). Taylor’s generated operation remains distinct from the historical proposition.

## Selected passages

<a id="owen-1843-comparative-anatomy-q001"></a>
### q001 — Analogue

**Paraphrase:** The definition identifies an analogue by an organ or part serving the same function in a different animal.

**Locator:** Glossary, printed p.374; PDF page376.

**Verification:** embedded text read and selected passage identified; no exact quotation or full-work collation claim.

<a id="owen-1843-comparative-anatomy-q002"></a>
### q002 — Homologue

**Paraphrase:** The definition identifies a homologue as the corresponding organ across animals despite variation in form and function. Read with the analogue entry, its anatomical criterion is distinct from shared function; neither definition itself establishes a modern common-descent criterion.

**Locator:** Glossary, printed p.379; PDF page381.

**Verification:** embedded text read and selected passage identified; no exact quotation or full-work collation claim.
